Each switch is off unless you turn it on: Each switch is off unless you turn it on. What it sends is below it; the privacy page on playhorizon.dev says how long it is kept.
After each session: frame-time percentil: After each session: frame-time percentiles and a 14-bucket histogram, tick times, peak memory and startup times, with your machine (OS, CPU and its cores and clocks, memory size, GPU, its memory and driver, drive type, screen size and refresh rate, laptop or desktop, on battery or not) and the settings that change performance.
When the game crashes: the error, where: When the game crashes: the error, where in Horizon's code it happened, your graphics adapter and settings. No log, no world or server, no user name in paths.

Never sent: your account name or UUID, w: Never sent: your account name or UUID, world names, server addresses, chat, or your IP address. Each report is dated to the day, under a random install ID you can delete.
While you play, the game sends an anonym: While you play, the game sends an anonymous "I'm playing" ping once a minute, so the launcher can show how many people play Horizon right now. It holds: a random number made when the game starts and forgotten when it closes, the Horizon version, your OS (Linux, macOS or Windows), and whether you have a world open to LAN or friends. It doesn't hold: your account, your install ID, world or server names, or anything you do in the game, and the server doesn't keep your IP address. It is sent whatever the switches say.
